tokenit.KUVAUS: Guided demonstration project: build and publish a hand-coded HTML, CSS and JavaScript site with Bootstrap that presents the Ionian language, week by week, from 31 Aug to 4 Dec 2026.
tokenit.LEAD: You created a language. In this project you build the website that presents it: hand-written HTML, CSS and JavaScript where every grammar table comes from a JSON file, Bootstrap gives you the components and the number converter is built from scratch, and the result is published for real learners. You work one week at a time on this page, keep your project journal here, and push every work sample to your Git repository. The demonstration assesses your web development skills — the language itself is your own source material.
tokenit.POLKU_H2: The site is built one view at a time
tokenit.POLKU_OHJE: it tells you what exists after the week that did not exist before.
tokenit.POLKU_KUVA_ALT: The four phases: Foundations, Grammar views, Finish, Release
tokenit.POLKU_KUVA_TEKSTI: Foundations first, then the grammar views, then quality and testing, and finally the release and the demonstration.
tokenit.HERO_KUVA_ALT: Weekly workflow: site map, component, data, test, publish
tokenit.HERO_KUVA_TEKSTI: Pick a task, build the component, feed it data, test it, publish it.
tokenit.TYOMAA_TEKSTI: The real work happens in your local repository: the page files in the root, css/ and js/ for your own code, data/ for the language data (JSON), tests/ for the unit tests.
tokenit.TYOMAA_LISA: A local web server (Live Server) shows changes instantly — fetch() will not read data/ over file://.
tokenit.KANSIOT: css/, js/, data/, tests/ and project-docs/
tokenit.JULKAISULAUSE: The repository is public — never commit personal data.
tokenit.TOIMEKSIANTO_OTSIKKO: A website for a language that exists nowhere else
tokenit.JALKI_VAATIMUS: Explores the possibilities and limits of the component library (k2)
tokenit.JALKI_ISSUE: #7 Compare Bootstrap against the alternatives for the grammar tables
tokenit.JALKI_VALMIS: Memo lists possibilities, limits and own measurements for 3 options
tokenit.JALKI_TESTI: Comparison memo in project-docs/, decision in the plan, Bootstrap configured in css/style.css in a commit
tokenit.SUUNNITELMA_EYEBROW: Technical plan · fill in during weeks 36–37
tokenit.SUUNNITELMA_JOHDANTO: The pre-filled sections come from the brief. You write the decisions that are yours: goal, audience, which Bootstrap components you build on, scope. The supervisor owns the open items — do not decide those yourself or with AI.
tokenit.SUUNNITELMA_AJOITUS: Draft it in week 36, finish it by the end of week 37, and update it when the supervisor answers an open item.
tokenit.SUUNNITELMA_KUVA_ALT: The plan has three parts: goal and audience, my decisions, site map
tokenit.SUUNNITELMA_KUVA_OTSIKKO: The plan comes before the code.
tokenit.SUUNNITELMA_KUVA_TEKSTI: Goal, audience and site map first — then the first component.
tokenit.OMAT_PAATOKSET_TEKSTI: Fill these in yourself. Each decision is tested in your own work during the named weeks.
tokenit.KICKOFF_KARKI: By the end of the first phase an empty but real site is live at your public URL.
tokenit.PAIVA1: Read the brief, underline the requirements and write down every unclear point as a question for the kickoff talk.
tokenit.PAIVA2: Agree the scope: which views are P0, what is explicitly out (the conjugator!), and who reviews the site in week 44.
tokenit.PAIVA3: Install VS Code and Live Server, create the site folder, serve it over http://localhost and open it from your phone over the local network.
tokenit.PAIVA4: Draft the technical plan from the pre-filled sections and split the P0 work into GitHub issues.
tokenit.PAIVA5: Publish the empty site to GitHub Pages from the main branch and verify the public URL works on another device. First commit, first deploy — the publishing path exists.
tokenit.TESTI_KUVA_ALT: Testing loop: plan the test, run it, find the bug, fix, re-test
tokenit.AI_JOHDANTO: AI may help you with HTML, CSS and JavaScript, error messages and test ideas — logged, verified and tested. It cannot help you with the content: no model knows Ionian. Every grammar table, every phrase and every expected test result comes from your own PDF and is checked against it. The site structure, the accessibility solutions and the number converter logic are your own work — that is what the demonstration assesses.
tokenit.AI_KUVA_ALT: The four steps of AI use: ask, verify, test, log
tokenit.AI_KOHDE: your own data model and pages
tokenit.AI_LAHDE: MDN, the official Bootstrap documentation and your own PDF
tokenit.AI_ESIM_KYSYMYS: Why does my fetch fail when I open the page as a file:// URL?
tokenit.AI_ESIM_KAYTTO: Used the local-server explanation, rejected the suggested innerHTML rendering
tokenit.AI_ESIM_TARKISTUS: Served the folder over http://localhost, table renders — learned why fetch needs a server

koonti.kuvaus: Opiskelija esittelee itse luomansa kielen: käsin kirjoitettu HTML/CSS/JS-sivusto, jossa Bootstrap on komponenttikirjastona, kielioppitaulukot tulevat JSON-datasta fetchillä, numeromuunnin on rakennettu itse alusta ilman kirjastoa ja tuotos julkaistaan GitHub Pagesiin. Ei käännösvaihetta eikä bundleria. Koko projekti englanniksi.
